name: Al-Isrā
meaning: The Night Journey (Al-Isra) - also famously known in early Hadith collections as Surah Bani Israel (The Children of Israel).
revelation_details: Makkan (111 verses, revealed in Makkah shortly before the migration to Madinah, following the miraculous Night Journey).
core_theme: This Surah is a breathtaking transition from deep earthly grief to heavenly honor. Revealed after the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) endured his hardest year of personal loss and fierce rejection, it opens by glorifying Allah for taking him from Makkah to Jerusalem in a single night. Alongside a comprehensive moral charter for human society - covering kindness to parents, justice, modesty, and honesty - it recounts pivotal stories of the Children of Israel, the rebellion of Iblis, Prophet Musa's nine miracles, and the ultimate honor awaiting Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) on the Day of Judgment.
name_origin:
The Surah takes its primary name, Al-Isra ("The Night Journey"), from its very first verse, which records the miraculous nighttime journey of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) from Al-Masjid al-Haram in Makkah to Al-Masjid al-Aqsa in Jerusalem. It is also widely called Surah Bani Israel by the companions because verses 2-8 recount the rise and fall of the Children of Israel.

The Historical Context (Honor After Heartbreak): To feel the true power of this Surah, you have to look at what Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) had just endured. This period is known in Islamic history as the Year of Sorrow ('Am al-Huzn). Within a short span, the Prophet (pbuh) lost his beloved wife and closest supporter, Khadijah (RA), and his protective uncle, Abu Talib. When he traveled to the city of Ta'if hoping they would accept Islam, the leaders mocked him and sent mobs to stone him until his shoes filled with blood.

When the doors of the earth seemed completely shut against him, Allah opened the doors of the heavens. By taking the Prophet (pbuh) to Jerusalem and ascending him through the seven heavens, Allah comforted his broken heart and showed that leadership of pure monotheism had officially passed to Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and his Ummah.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Miraculous Night Journey (Al-Isra)

points.label: Glorifying Allah
points.detail: The chapter begins with Subhana (Glory be to Allah), highlighting His absolute power to do what no human or creation can ever do.

points.label: From Makkah to Jerusalem
points.detail: Allah took His servant, Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم), by night from Al-Masjid al-Haram (the Sacred Mosque in Makkah) to Al-Masjid al-Aqsa (the Farthest Mosque in Jerusalem), whose surroundings Allah has blessed spiritually and materially.

points.label: Showing Great Signs
points.detail: The purpose of this miraculous journey was to show the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) some of Allah's greatest signs, affirming that Allah is the All-Hearing and All-Seeing.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Glorifying Allah: The chapter begins with Subhana (Glory be to Allah), highlighting His absolute power to do what no human or creation can ever do.
• From Makkah to Jerusalem: Allah took His servant, Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم), by night from Al-Masjid al-Haram (the Sacred Mosque in Makkah) to Al-Masjid al-Aqsa (the Farthest Mosque in Jerusalem), whose surroundings Allah has blessed spiritually and materially.
• Showing Great Signs: The purpose of this miraculous journey was to show the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) some of Allah's greatest signs, affirming that Allah is the All-Hearing and All-Seeing.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Classical scholars like Ibn Kathir note that referring to the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) as 'Abdihi (His servant) in this moment of highest honor shows that true servitude to Allah is the greatest rank a human can achieve. Connecting Makkah and Jerusalem in a single night also linked the final Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) to the entire legacy of earlier prophets, whom he led in prayer at Al-Masjid al-Aqsa.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Prophet Musa (AS) and the Two Corruptions of the Children of Israel

points.label: The Torah and Pure Reliance
points.detail: Allah gave Prophet Musa (AS) the Book (Torah) as guidance for the Children of Israel, commanding them never to take any protector or disposer of affairs besides Allah, reminding them that they are descendants of the grateful believers saved with Prophet Nuh (AS).

points.label: Two Decrees of Corruption
points.detail: Allah decreed in their scripture that the Children of Israel would cause great corruption on earth twice and rise to extreme arrogance.

points.label: Consequence and Return
points.detail: When the first corruption occurred, Allah sent mighty servants against them who entered their homes and overpowered them. Later, Allah returned power, wealth, and children to them. When the second corruption occurred, enemies were again sent to disgrace them, enter the Masjid as before, and destroy what they had built.

points.label: The Door of Mercy
points.detail: Allah reminds them that He may still have mercy on them if they repent - but if they return to corruption, He will return to punishment, and Hell is prepared as a prison for disbelievers.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• The Torah and Pure Reliance: Allah gave Prophet Musa (AS) the Book (Torah) as guidance for the Children of Israel, commanding them never to take any protector or disposer of affairs besides Allah, reminding them that they are descendants of the grateful believers saved with Prophet Nuh (AS).
• Two Decrees of Corruption: Allah decreed in their scripture that the Children of Israel would cause great corruption on earth twice and rise to extreme arrogance.
• Consequence and Return: When the first corruption occurred, Allah sent mighty servants against them who entered their homes and overpowered them. Later, Allah returned power, wealth, and children to them. When the second corruption occurred, enemies were again sent to disgrace them, enter the Masjid as before, and destroy what they had built.
• The Door of Mercy: Allah reminds them that He may still have mercy on them if they repent - but if they return to corruption, He will return to punishment, and Hell is prepared as a prison for disbelievers.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Tafsir scholars such as Ibn Kathir and As-Sa'di explain that these verses establish a universal law of history: spiritual privilege and noble ancestry do not protect any community from downfall if it falls into arrogance and injustice. At the same time, Allah's promise - "if you do good, you do good for yourselves" - shows that every nation holds the key to its own rise or ruin.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Quran's Guidance and Human Impatience

points.label: The Most Upright Path
points.detail: This Quran guides to what is most upright and gives glad tidings to believers who do righteous deeds that they will receive a great reward, while warning those who deny the Hereafter of a painful punishment.

points.label: Praying for Harm in Anger
points.detail: Humans often pray for evil upon themselves, their families, or their wealth in moments of anger just as eagerly as they pray for good - because human beings are naturally hasty.

points.label: Signs of Night and Day
points.detail: Allah made the night and the day as two clear signs: He erased the light of the night for rest and made the day bright so people can seek Allah's bounty, calculate years, and keep track of time.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• The Most Upright Path: This Quran guides to what is most upright and gives glad tidings to believers who do righteous deeds that they will receive a great reward, while warning those who deny the Hereafter of a painful punishment.
• Praying for Harm in Anger: Humans often pray for evil upon themselves, their families, or their wealth in moments of anger just as eagerly as they pray for good - because human beings are naturally hasty.
• Signs of Night and Day: Allah made the night and the day as two clear signs: He erased the light of the night for rest and made the day bright so people can seek Allah's bounty, calculate years, and keep track of time.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Classical commentators explain that verse 11 is a practical warning for everyday life: when parents or individuals lose their temper, they sometimes utter curses or harsh prayers they do not truly mean. Allah's mercy protects people from having their hasty, angry words answered, teaching believers to guard their tongues and practice patience.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Personal Accountability and the Law of Destroying Cities

points.label: Every Person's Record
points.detail: Allah has fastened every human's deeds to their own neck. On the Day of Resurrection, each person will be handed an open book of their life and told: "Read your own book! Today, your own soul is sufficient as a reckoner against you.

points.label: No One Carries Another's Sin
points.detail: Whoever chooses guidance does so for their own benefit, and whoever goes astray harms only themselves. No soul will ever bear the burden of another's sin.

points.label: Justice Before Punishment
points.detail: Allah never punishes a people until He first sends a messenger to make the truth clear.

points.label: How Cities Fall
points.detail: When Allah decrees the destruction of a town, its wealthy, privileged leaders indulge in open defiance and corruption, sealing the decree of destruction - just as many generations were destroyed after Prophet Nuh (AS).

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Every Person's Record: Allah has fastened every human's deeds to their own neck. On the Day of Resurrection, each person will be handed an open book of their life and told: "Read your own book! Today, your own soul is sufficient as a reckoner against you."
• No One Carries Another's Sin: Whoever chooses guidance does so for their own benefit, and whoever goes astray harms only themselves. No soul will ever bear the burden of another's sin.
• Justice Before Punishment: Allah never punishes a people until He first sends a messenger to make the truth clear.
• How Cities Fall: When Allah decrees the destruction of a town, its wealthy, privileged leaders indulge in open defiance and corruption, sealing the decree of destruction - just as many generations were destroyed after Prophet Nuh (AS).
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Imam al-Qurtubi and Ibn Kathir highlight the profound sense of personal responsibility here: on Judgment Day, no one can blame their family, society, or friends. Reading one's own book of deeds leaves zero room for excuses, reminding believers to write a record they will not be ashamed to read before Allah.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Seeking This World vs. Seeking the Hereafter

points.label: The Temporary World
points.detail: Whoever desires only this fleeting worldly life, Allah may quickly grant whatever He wills to whomever He wills - yet afterward, He assigns Hell for them, where they enter disgraced and rejected.

points.label: The Lasting Hereafter
points.detail: Whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it sincerely while being a true believer, their effort will be deeply appreciated and rewarded by Allah.

points.label: Equal Worldly Provision, Different Ranks
points.detail: Allah freely provides worldly sustenance to both groups, for the generosity of your Lord is never restricted. Yet in the Hereafter, the differences in rank and honor will be far greater.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• The Temporary World: Whoever desires only this fleeting worldly life, Allah may quickly grant whatever He wills to whomever He wills - yet afterward, He assigns Hell for them, where they enter disgraced and rejected.
• The Lasting Hereafter: Whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it sincerely while being a true believer, their effort will be deeply appreciated and rewarded by Allah.
• Equal Worldly Provision, Different Ranks: Allah freely provides worldly sustenance to both groups, for the generosity of your Lord is never restricted. Yet in the Hereafter, the differences in rank and honor will be far greater.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Tafsir scholars note three essential conditions for success in verse 19: wanting the Hereafter, actively striving for it with righteous deeds, and having true faith (iman). Mere wishes without action are not enough, and action without sincere faith does not last.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Pure Monotheism and Utmost Kindness to Parents

points.label: Worship Allah Alone
points.detail: Do not set up any other deity alongside Allah, or you will sit disgraced and forsaken.

points.label: Excellence to Parents
points.detail: Allah has decreed that you worship none but Him, and that you be deeply kind and dutiful to your parents. If one or both of them reach old age in your care, do not even say "Uff" (the slightest sound of annoyance) to them, nor scold them - instead, speak to them with noble, respectful words.

points.label: Humility and Prayer for Parents
points.detail: Lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy, and pray: "My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up when I was small.

points.label: Allah Knows Your Heart
points.detail: Your Lord knows best what is inside your hearts; if you are sincere and righteous, He is truly Forgiving to those who repeatedly turn back to Him.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Worship Allah Alone: Do not set up any other deity alongside Allah, or you will sit disgraced and forsaken.
• Excellence to Parents: Allah has decreed that you worship none but Him, and that you be deeply kind and dutiful to your parents. If one or both of them reach old age in your care, do not even say "Uff" (the slightest sound of annoyance) to them, nor scold them - instead, speak to them with noble, respectful words.
• Humility and Prayer for Parents: Lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy, and pray: "My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up when I was small."
• Allah Knows Your Heart: Your Lord knows best what is inside your hearts; if you are sincere and righteous, He is truly Forgiving to those who repeatedly turn back to Him.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Classical commentators emphasize how Allah placed kindness to parents immediately after worshipping Him alone - showing that honoring parents is the highest human right in Islam. Forbidding even the tiny sigh "Uff" when parents grow old and dependent teaches us that true devotion is tested not when caring for them is easy, but when it requires patience and gentleness.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Rights of Relatives, Avoiding Waste, and Balanced Spending

points.label: Give People Their Rights
points.detail: Give your close relatives their due rights, as well as the needy and the stranded traveler - and do not spend wastefully.

points.label: The Evil of Extravagance
points.detail: Those who squander wealth wastefully are described as the brothers of the devils, and Shaytan has always been deeply ungrateful to his Lord.

points.label: Kind Words When You Cannot Give
points.detail: If you have to turn away from those in need because you currently have nothing to give, speak to them with gentle, comforting words.

points.label: The Middle Path in Spending
points.detail: Do not tie your hand tightly to your neck (being stingy), nor stretch it out completely (spending recklessly), lest you end up blamed and empty-handed. Allah expands and restricts provision for whomever He wills with full knowledge of His servants.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Give People Their Rights: Give your close relatives their due rights, as well as the needy and the stranded traveler - and do not spend wastefully.
• The Evil of Extravagance: Those who squander wealth wastefully are described as the brothers of the devils, and Shaytan has always been deeply ungrateful to his Lord.
• Kind Words When You Cannot Give: If you have to turn away from those in need because you currently have nothing to give, speak to them with gentle, comforting words.
• The Middle Path in Spending: Do not tie your hand tightly to your neck (being stingy), nor stretch it out completely (spending recklessly), lest you end up blamed and empty-handed. Allah expands and restricts provision for whomever He wills with full knowledge of His servants.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Ibn Kathir explains that Islam teaches financial balance rather than extremes: stinginess hardens the heart and harms the community, while wasteful spending (tabdhir) - spending on sin or throwing away blessings - destroys gratitude. Even when a believer's wallet is empty, a gentle, respectful word is itself a form of charity.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Protecting Life, Chastity, Orphans, Promises, and Honest Trade

points.label: Do Not Kill Children Out of Fear of Poverty
points.detail: Allah strictly forbids killing children out of fear of poverty, assuring parents: "We provide for them and for you." Killing them is a massive sin.

points.label: Stay Far Away From Zina
points.detail: Do not even come near unlawful sexual relations (zina), for it is a shameful act and an evil path.

points.label: Sanctity of Human Life
points.detail: Never take any life that Allah has made sacred except through rightful justice. If someone is killed unjustly, Allah has given their heir the right to seek justice, while forbidding them from exceeding the limits in retaliation.

points.label: Protect the Orphan's Wealth
points.detail: Do not touch an orphan's property except in the best way that protects or grows it until they reach maturity.

points.label: Honor Covenants and Fair Trade
points.detail: Fulfill every promise and covenant, for every covenant will be questioned on Judgment Day. Give full measure and weigh with an honest, accurate scale - that is better and brings the finest outcome.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Do Not Kill Children Out of Fear of Poverty: Allah strictly forbids killing children out of fear of poverty, assuring parents: "We provide for them and for you." Killing them is a massive sin.
• Stay Far Away From Zina: Do not even come near unlawful sexual relations (zina), for it is a shameful act and an evil path.
• Sanctity of Human Life: Never take any life that Allah has made sacred except through rightful justice. If someone is killed unjustly, Allah has given their heir the right to seek justice, while forbidding them from exceeding the limits in retaliation.
• Protect the Orphan's Wealth: Do not touch an orphan's property except in the best way that protects or grows it until they reach maturity.
• Honor Covenants and Fair Trade: Fulfill every promise and covenant, for every covenant will be questioned on Judgment Day. Give full measure and weigh with an honest, accurate scale - that is better and brings the finest outcome.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Tafsir scholars notice the remarkable wording in verse 32: Allah does not merely say "do not commit zina," He says "do not even come near it." This closes every doorway that leads to immorality - such as immodesty, reckless mixing, and guarding one's gaze. Together, these verses build a safe, just society where life, family, orphans, and business transactions are fiercely protected.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Responsibility of the Senses, Humility, and Summary of Wisdom

points.label: Do Not Follow What You Do Not Know
points.detail: Do not speak about, accuse, or follow things of which you have no certain knowledge. Indeed, your hearing, your sight, and your heart will all be questioned on the Day of Judgment.

points.label: Walk With Humility
points.detail: Do not walk upon the earth with arrogance and pride - for you can never tear the earth apart, nor can you ever reach the height of the mountains.

points.label: Wisdom Revealed
points.detail: All of these forbidden traits are hateful to your Lord, and these commandments are part of the wisdom (hikmah) that Allah has revealed to the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم). The section closes as it began: never set up another deity with Allah, lest you be thrown into Hell blamed and cast out.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Do Not Follow What You Do Not Know: Do not speak about, accuse, or follow things of which you have no certain knowledge. Indeed, your hearing, your sight, and your heart will all be questioned on the Day of Judgment.
• Walk With Humility: Do not walk upon the earth with arrogance and pride - for you can never tear the earth apart, nor can you ever reach the height of the mountains.
• Wisdom Revealed: All of these forbidden traits are hateful to your Lord, and these commandments are part of the wisdom (hikmah) that Allah has revealed to the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم). The section closes as it began: never set up another deity with Allah, lest you be thrown into Hell blamed and cast out.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Classical scholars highlight verse 36 as the ultimate ethical rule against gossip, rumors, and speaking without proof. Remembering that our own eyes, ears, and hearts will testify before Allah inspires deep mindfulness in what we watch, listen to, and share with others.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Refuting False Claims About Angels and Universal Glorification

points.label: Refuting Pagan Beliefs
points.detail: Allah rebukes the polytheists who claimed that angels were Allah's daughters while preferring sons for themselves - calling it a grave, outrageous statement.

points.label: One Supreme Sovereign
points.detail: Allah asks: if there were other gods alongside Him as they claim, those gods would have sought a way to challenge the Owner of the Throne. Glory be to Him, far above what they say!

points.label: Everything Glorifies Allah
points.detail: The seven heavens, the earth, and everything within them glorify Allah. There is not a single thing in existence except that it glorifies Him with His praise - though humans do not understand their glorification. Truly, Allah is Most Forbearing and Forgiving.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Refuting Pagan Beliefs: Allah rebukes the polytheists who claimed that angels were Allah's daughters while preferring sons for themselves - calling it a grave, outrageous statement.
• One Supreme Sovereign: Allah asks: if there were other gods alongside Him as they claim, those gods would have sought a way to challenge the Owner of the Throne. Glory be to Him, far above what they say!
• Everything Glorifies Allah: The seven heavens, the earth, and everything within them glorify Allah. There is not a single thing in existence except that it glorifies Him with His praise - though humans do not understand their glorification. Truly, Allah is Most Forbearing and Forgiving.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Ibn Kathir and As-Sa'di note the awe-inspiring truth in verse 44: every tree, rock, bird, and star is constantly praising its Creator in its own way. Realizing that the entire universe is in a state of dhikr (remembrance of Allah) encourages the believer to join creation in praising Him rather than remaining heedless.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Unseen Barrier and Mockery of Resurrection

points.label: A Hidden Barrier
points.detail: When the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) recites the Quran, Allah places an invisible veil between him and those who refuse to believe in the Hereafter, along with coverings over their hearts and deafness in their ears so they turn away in aversion when Allah alone is mentioned.

points.label: Mocking the Prophet
points.detail: Allah knows best how they listen only to mock, whispering privately to one another that the believers are merely following a "bewitched man.

points.label: Doubting Resurrection
points.detail: They ask in disbelief, "When we have become dry bones and dust, will we really be raised up as a new creation?

points.label: The Unstoppable Answer
points.detail: Allah commands the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) to reply: "Be stones or iron - or any creation you think is even harder to bring to life!" When they ask, "Who will bring us back?" say: "The One who created you the very first time!" Even when they shake their heads mockingly and ask, "When will that be?" say: "Perhaps it is very soon - the Day He calls you, and you will answer praising Him, thinking you stayed in this world only a little while.

• A Hidden Barrier: When the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) recites the Quran, Allah places an invisible veil between him and those who refuse to believe in the Hereafter, along with coverings over their hearts and deafness in their ears so they turn away in aversion when Allah alone is mentioned.
• Mocking the Prophet: Allah knows best how they listen only to mock, whispering privately to one another that the believers are merely following a "bewitched man."
• Doubting Resurrection: They ask in disbelief, "When we have become dry bones and dust, will we really be raised up as a new creation?"
• The Unstoppable Answer: Allah commands the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) to reply: "Be stones or iron - or any creation you think is even harder to bring to life!" When they ask, "Who will bring us back?" say: "The One who created you the very first time!" Even when they shake their heads mockingly and ask, "When will that be?" say: "Perhaps it is very soon - the Day He calls you, and you will answer praising Him, thinking you stayed in this world only a little while.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Tafsir scholars point out the sharp logic of verse 51: creating life from scratch the very first time is no easier or harder for Allah than bringing bones, stones, or iron back to life. What feels impossible to the limited human mind is effortless for the Creator of the universe.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Speaking the Best Words and the Helplessness of False Gods

points.label: Speak the Best Words
points.detail: Allah commands His servants to speak only what is best and kindest, warning that Shaytan constantly tries to sow discord and hatred between people - for Shaytan is a clear enemy to humanity.

points.label: Allah's Knowledge and Mercy
points.detail: Your Lord knows you best; if He wills, He shows you mercy, and if He wills, He punishes you. Every prophet was given distinct favors, just as Allah gave Prophet Dawud (AS) the Zabur (Psalms).

points.label: Even the Righteous Seek Allah's Nearness
points.detail: Tell the polytheists to call upon those they worship besides Allah - they have no power to remove harm or shift it away. In fact, the righteous beings (such as angels, prophets, or saints) whom some people wrongly worship are themselves striving to seek nearness (wasilah) to Allah, hoping for His mercy and fearing His punishment.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Speak the Best Words: Allah commands His servants to speak only what is best and kindest, warning that Shaytan constantly tries to sow discord and hatred between people - for Shaytan is a clear enemy to humanity.
• Allah's Knowledge and Mercy: Your Lord knows you best; if He wills, He shows you mercy, and if He wills, He punishes you. Every prophet was given distinct favors, just as Allah gave Prophet Dawud (AS) the Zabur (Psalms).
• Even the Righteous Seek Allah's Nearness: Tell the polytheists to call upon those they worship besides Allah - they have no power to remove harm or shift it away. In fact, the righteous beings (such as angels, prophets, or saints) whom some people wrongly worship are themselves striving to seek nearness (wasilah) to Allah, hoping for His mercy and fearing His punishment.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Verse 53 is a golden rule for healthy relationships and communities: choosing the best words - not merely acceptable ones - prevents Shaytan from turning small misunderstandings into bitter grudges. Meanwhile, verse 57 dismantles saint- and angel-worship completely: if even the closest servants of Allah are humbly begging for His mercy, only Allah Himself deserves to be worshipped.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Destroying Sinful Cities, Withheld Miracles, and the Test of the Night Journey

points.label: The Fate of Corrupt Towns
points.detail: There is no sinful town except that Allah will destroy it or punish it severely before the Day of Resurrection - all recorded in Allah's decree.

points.label: Why Physical Miracles Were Not Sent
points.detail: Allah explains that He refrained from sending the specific physical miracles demanded by the Quraysh only because earlier nations (like Thamud with the miraculous she-camel) rejected clear miracles and were immediately destroyed as a result. Allah sends signs solely to warn and awaken people.

points.label: The Vision and the Cursed Tree
points.detail: Allah reminds the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) that He surrounds all people with His knowledge, and that both the vision shown to him during the Night Journey (Al-Isra) and the "cursed tree" in the Quran (Zaqqum, the bitter tree in Hell) were made a trial (fitnah) to test people's faith - yet warnings only increased the stubborn disbelievers in arrogance.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• The Fate of Corrupt Towns: There is no sinful town except that Allah will destroy it or punish it severely before the Day of Resurrection - all recorded in Allah's decree.
• Why Physical Miracles Were Not Sent: Allah explains that He refrained from sending the specific physical miracles demanded by the Quraysh only because earlier nations (like Thamud with the miraculous she-camel) rejected clear miracles and were immediately destroyed as a result. Allah sends signs solely to warn and awaken people.
• The Vision and the Cursed Tree: Allah reminds the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) that He surrounds all people with His knowledge, and that both the vision shown to him during the Night Journey (Al-Isra) and the "cursed tree" in the Quran (Zaqqum, the bitter tree in Hell) were made a trial (fitnah) to test people's faith - yet warnings only increased the stubborn disbelievers in arrogance.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: In Sahih al-Bukhari (3888), Ibn Abbas (RA) explicitly affirmed that the "vision" in verse 60 was a real, physical sight shown to the Prophet's eyes during the Night Journey to Jerusalem, not a mere dream. When the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) reported it, people with weak faith mocked him, while true believers like Abu Bakr (RA) immediately believed - proving how divine signs separate sincere faith from stubborn skepticism.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Arrogance of Iblis and His Limit Over True Servants

points.label: Refusal to Prostrate
points.detail: When Allah commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam (AS), all obeyed except Iblis, who arrogantly asked, "Should I prostrate to one You created from clay?

points.label: Iblis's Threat
points.detail: Iblis asked Allah for respite until the Day of Resurrection, boasting that he would bring nearly all of Adam's descendants under his control except a few.

points.label: The Temptation and the Limit
points.detail: Allah told Iblis to go ahead and use his voice, his forces, and his influence over wealth and children to tempt whoever follows him - promising nothing but delusion. Yet Allah declared clearly: "Indeed, over My true servants you have no authority. And sufficient is your Lord as a Disposer of affairs.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Refusal to Prostrate: When Allah commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam (AS), all obeyed except Iblis, who arrogantly asked, "Should I prostrate to one You created from clay?"
• Iblis's Threat: Iblis asked Allah for respite until the Day of Resurrection, boasting that he would bring nearly all of Adam's descendants under his control except a few.
• The Temptation and the Limit: Allah told Iblis to go ahead and use his voice, his forces, and his influence over wealth and children to tempt whoever follows him - promising nothing but delusion. Yet Allah declared clearly: "Indeed, over My true servants you have no authority. And sufficient is your Lord as a Disposer of affairs.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Classical commentators explain that Shaytan's "voice" includes every call to disobedience, and his partnership in wealth and children refers to unlawful earnings and raising children away from Allah's guidance. Yet verse 65 brings complete reassurance: Shaytan can whisper, tempt, and deceive, but he can never force a sincere believer who relies on Allah.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Mercy at Sea, Human Ingratitude, and the Honor of Humanity

points.label: Sailing the Seas
points.detail: It is Allah who smoothly drives ships across the ocean so people can seek His bounty, out of His mercy.

points.label: Forgetting Allah on Dry Land
points.detail: When danger strikes at sea, everyone you used to call upon vanishes except Allah alone. Yet the moment He brings you safely back to land, you turn away - truly, humans are deeply ungrateful!

points.label: Warning of Sudden Return
points.detail: Do you feel safe that Allah will not cause the land to swallow you, send a storm of stones upon you, or send you back to sea to be drowned by a fierce wind?

points.label: The Dignity of Humanity
points.detail: Allah declares: "And We have certainly honored the children of Adam" - carrying them over land and sea, providing them with good, wholesome things, and favoring them clearly over much of His creation.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Sailing the Seas: It is Allah who smoothly drives ships across the ocean so people can seek His bounty, out of His mercy.
• Forgetting Allah on Dry Land: When danger strikes at sea, everyone you used to call upon vanishes except Allah alone. Yet the moment He brings you safely back to land, you turn away - truly, humans are deeply ungrateful!
• Warning of Sudden Return: Do you feel safe that Allah will not cause the land to swallow you, send a storm of stones upon you, or send you back to sea to be drowned by a fierce wind?
• The Dignity of Humanity: Allah declares: "And We have certainly honored the children of Adam" - carrying them over land and sea, providing them with good, wholesome things, and favoring them clearly over much of His creation.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Tafsir scholars note that verse 70 is a foundational charter of human dignity in Islam. Every human being - by virtue of being a child of Adam - is honored by Allah with intellect, upright form, speech, and stewardship on earth. Recognizing this honor should fill a person with gratitude, not ingratitude.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Judgment Day, Attempts to Tempt the Prophet, and Allah's Unchanging Law

points.label: Called With Their Record
points.detail: On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will summon every group of people along with their leader (or their book of deeds). Those given their record in their right hand will read it joyfully and will not be wronged by even a tiny thread on a date stone.

points.label: Spiritual Blindness
points.detail: Whoever lives spiritually blind to the truth in this world will be blind in the Hereafter and even further astray from the right path.

points.label: Resisting Compromise
points.detail: The disbelievers nearly tempted the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) to compromise on parts of revelation to please them. Had Allah not kept him firm, he might have leaned slightly toward them - which would have brought double punishment in life and death.

points.label: Expelling Messengers Brings Ruin
points.detail: They also plotted to drive the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) out of Makkah, but Allah warned that if they did, they would not remain after him except for a short while - for this has always been Allah's unchanging law (Sunnah) with earlier messengers.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Called With Their Record: On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will summon every group of people along with their leader (or their book of deeds). Those given their record in their right hand will read it joyfully and will not be wronged by even a tiny thread on a date stone.
• Spiritual Blindness: Whoever lives spiritually blind to the truth in this world will be blind in the Hereafter and even further astray from the right path.
• Resisting Compromise: The disbelievers nearly tempted the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) to compromise on parts of revelation to please them. Had Allah not kept him firm, he might have leaned slightly toward them - which would have brought double punishment in life and death.
• Expelling Messengers Brings Ruin: They also plotted to drive the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) out of Makkah, but Allah warned that if they did, they would not remain after him except for a short while - for this has always been Allah's unchanging law (Sunnah) with earlier messengers.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Ibn Kathir explains that verses 73-75 teach a vital lesson for every generation: truth cannot be compromised to win popularity or avoid opposition. Even the noblest of creation, Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم), relied on Allah's steadfastness (tathbit) to stay firm - reminding believers to constantly ask Allah to keep their hearts firm upon His religion.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Daily Prayers, Tahajjud, the Praised Station, and the Quran as Healing

points.label: The Five Daily Prayers
points.detail: Establish the prayer from the decline of the sun at midday until the darkness of the night (covering Zuhr, 'Asr, Maghrib, and 'Isha), and recite the Quran at dawn (Fajr) - for the dawn prayer is directly witnessed by the angels.

points.label: Tahajjud and Maqam Mahmud
points.detail: Rise during part of the night for the voluntary Tahajjud prayer as an extra devotion, so that your Lord may raise you to Maqam Mahmud (the Praised Station).

points.label: A Prayer for Every Transition
points.detail: Pray: "My Lord, let my entry be a true, sound entry and my exit be a true, sound exit, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority.

points.label: Truth Prevails
points.detail: Declare: "Truth has come, and falsehood has vanished. Indeed, falsehood is bound to vanish.

points.label: Healing and Mercy
points.detail: Allah sends down in the Quran that which is a healing (shifa') and a mercy for the believers, while it only increases the wrongdoers in loss.

points.label: Human Mood Swings
points.detail: When Allah blesses a person, they often turn away in pride; when hardship touches them, they fall into despair. Every person acts according to their own character, and Allah knows best who is rightly guided.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:

• Human Mood Swings: When Allah blesses a person, they often turn away in pride; when hardship touches them, they fall into despair. Every person acts according to their own character, and Allah knows best who is rightly guided.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Authentic Hadiths illuminate this passage richly: in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) taught that the angels of the night and the angels of the day meet together at Fajr prayer, making it uniquely witnessed. Likewise, in Jami' at-Tirmidhi (3137) and Sahih al-Bukhari, Maqam Mahmud is identified as the Grand Intercession (Ash-Shafa'ah al-'Uzma) granted exclusively to Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) on the Day of Judgment when all other prophets decline. And the Quran is described as a true healing - curing both spiritual diseases of the heart (like doubt and anxiety) and physical ailments by Allah's permission.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Question About the Soul (Ar-Ruh) and the Unmatched Quran

points.label: The Nature of the Soul
points.detail: People ask the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) about the Ruh (the soul/spirit). Allah commands him to reply: "The Ruh is from the affair (command) of my Lord, and humanity has been given only a tiny amount of knowledge.

points.label: Revelation Is Pure Mercy
points.detail: If Allah willed, He could take away everything He revealed to the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم), and no one could protect it - keeping it is purely a mercy from Allah, whose favor upon the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) is immense.

points.label: The Ultimate Challenge
points.detail: Declare: "If all of mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Quran, they could never produce anything like it, even if they backed each other up.

points.label: Every Kind of Example
points.detail: Allah has explained every kind of lesson and parable in this Quran for humanity, yet most people stubbornly insist on disbelief.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:

• The Ultimate Challenge: Declare: "If all of mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Quran, they could never produce anything like it, even if they backed each other up."
• Every Kind of Example: Allah has explained every kind of lesson and parable in this Quran for humanity, yet most people stubbornly insist on disbelief.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: In Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA) narrated that when some people in Madinah asked the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) about the Ruh, he stood silent while receiving revelation, then recited verse 85. This verse humbles human intellect: despite all our scientific progress, we still cannot grasp the exact essence of the very soul keeping us alive, reminding us how small human knowledge is compared to Allah's infinite knowledge.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Stubborn Demands for Miracles and Why Messengers Are Human

points.label: Endless Excuses
points.detail: The disbelievers arrogantly demanded: "We will never believe in you until you make a spring gush from the earth for us, or have a garden of palms and grapes with rivers flowing through it, or make the sky fall on us in pieces, or bring Allah and the angels face to face before us, or have a house of gold, or climb up to heaven and bring back a physical book we can read!

points.label: I Am Only a Human Messenger
points.detail: Allah told the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) to reply: "Glory be to my Lord! Am I anything other than a human messenger?

points.label: Why Not an Angel Messenger?
points.detail: Nothing stopped people from believing when guidance came except their complaint: "Has Allah sent a mere human as a messenger?" Allah explains: if angels were walking peacefully on earth as its inhabitants, He would have sent an angel from heaven as their messenger - but for humans, He sends a human role model.

points.label: Allah Is Sufficient as Witness
points.detail: Say: "Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you. Truly, He is All-Aware and All-Seeing of His servants.

• Allah Is Sufficient as Witness: Say: "Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you. Truly, He is All-Aware and All-Seeing of His servants.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Tafsir scholars explain the deep wisdom in verse 95: a prophet's mission is not just to recite words, but to live as a practical example of how to worship, endure hardship, love family, and deal fairly with people. An angel who does not eat, sleep, feel hunger, or face human emotions could never serve as a relatable role model for human beings.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: True Guidance, Gathering on Judgment Day, and Human Stinginess

points.label: Guidance Is in Allah's Hands
points.detail: Whoever Allah guides is truly guided, and whoever He leaves to stray will find no protectors besides Him.

points.label: A Humiliating Gathering
points.detail: On the Day of Resurrection, stubborn disbelievers will be gathered on their faces - blind, dumb, and deaf - with Hellfire as their home; whenever its flames subside, Allah increases its blaze.

points.label: Proof of Resurrection
points.detail: That is their punishment for denying Allah's signs and mocking resurrection. Do they not see that Allah, who created the vast heavens and the earth, is easily able to create the likes of them again and has set a clear, undoubted term for them?

points.label: Human Stinginess
points.detail: Say: "Even if you possessed the infinite treasuries of the mercy of my Lord, you would still hold back out of fear of spending them!" Truly, human beings are naturally stingy.

verse_breakdowns.reflection: Classical commentators highlight how verse 100 contrasts human scarcity-mindset with Allah's infinite generosity. Even if a person owned limitless wealth, human fear and selfishness would still tempt them to hoard it - whereas Allah gives endlessly to all creation without His treasuries ever decreasing.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Prophet Musa (AS), the Nine Clear Signs, and Pharaoh's Downfall

points.label: Nine Clear Signs
points.detail: Allah gave Prophet Musa (AS) nine unmistakable miracles (such as the staff, the shining hand, the years of famine, locusts, lice, frogs, blood, etc.) to prove his message.

points.label: Pharaoh's Denial and Musa's Reply
points.detail: When Musa (AS) came to Pharaoh, Pharaoh arrogantly dismissed him, saying, "I think you are bewitched, O Musa!" Musa (AS) calmly replied, "You know very well that none sent these signs down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as clear proofs - and I truly think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed to ruin.

points.label: Drowning of Pharaoh
points.detail: Pharaoh tried to wipe out Musa and his people from the land, so Allah drowned Pharaoh and everyone with him, and then settled the Children of Israel in the land - reminding them that when the promise of the Hereafter arrives, Allah will gather all of humanity together.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:

• Pharaoh's Denial and Musa's Reply: When Musa (AS) came to Pharaoh, Pharaoh arrogantly dismissed him, saying, "I think you are bewitched, O Musa!" Musa (AS) calmly replied, "You know very well that none sent these signs down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as clear proofs - and I truly think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed to ruin."

verse_breakdowns.reflection: Ibn Kathir notes that placing Pharaoh's story near the end of the Surah directly connects to the Makkan disbelievers' demands in verses 90-93. Pharaoh was shown nine massive, undeniable physical miracles right before his eyes, yet his arrogance still made him call Musa (AS) "bewitched" - proving once again that miracles alone never cure an arrogant heart.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Gradual Revelation, Calling on Allah's Beautiful Names, and Praising Him Alone

points.label: Revealed in Truth and Stages
points.detail: Allah sent down the Quran in pure truth, and revealed it gradually in portions so the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) could recite it calmly to people over time.

points.label: The Tears of the Knowledgeable

Those who were given true knowledge before it fall down upon their faces in prostration when it is recited to them, saying: "Glory be to our Lord! Truly, our Lord's promise has been fulfilled." They fall on their faces weeping, and it increases them in humility.

points.label: Calling Upon Allah's Beautiful Names
points.detail: Say: "Call upon Allah, or call upon Ar-Rahman (the Most Merciful). Whichever name you call upon, to Him belong the Most Beautiful Names (Al-Asma' al-Husna).

points.label: Moderation in Prayer
points.detail: Neither raise your voice too loudly in your prayer nor whisper it silently, but seek a balanced middle path between the two.

points.label: The Majestic Closing Praise (Verse 111)

verse_breakdowns.reflection: Classical scholars point out the stunning symmetry of Surah Al-Isra: it opens with Subhana (glorifying Allah for His absolute perfection) and closes with Alhamdulillah and Takbir (praising and magnifying Him above any son, partner, or weakness). Authentic Tafsir narrations explain that verse 110 was revealed in Makkah when the polytheists mocked the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) upon hearing him call on both Allah and Ar-Rahman, thinking he was calling on two different gods - so Allah taught believers to call on all His Beautiful Names and to recite prayers in a balanced, moderate tone.

stories_in_surah.title: The Epic Stories and Historical Events of Surah Al-Isra
stories_in_surah.content: According to classical scholars of Tafsir (such as Ibn Kathir, Al-Tabari, and Al-Qurtubi) and authentic Hadith collections, these are the detailed accounts of the major stories and historical moments found in this chapter:

stories_in_surah.title: Prophet Musa (AS), the Nine Clear Signs, and Pharaoh's Drowning (Verses 101-104)
stories_in_surah.content:
Right after the pagan Quraysh arrogantly demanded physical miracles from Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) - such as making springs gush from the earth, building a house of gold, or climbing to heaven to bring back a physical book - Allah tells the story of Pharaoh to prove that miracles never cure an arrogant heart.

The Tafsir Details: Allah gave Prophet Musa (AS) nine unmistakable signs (classical commentators like Ibn Abbas and Ibn Kathir list them as the staff turning into a serpent, the shining white hand, the years of famine, the shortage of crops, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the water turning to blood).

Despite witnessing these massive miracles right before his eyes, Pharaoh arrogantly dismissed Musa (AS), saying: "Indeed, I think you, O Musa, are bewitched!" Musa (AS) looked straight at him and exposed the truth inside Pharaoh's own heart: "You have already known that none has sent down these [signs] except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as clear evidence, and indeed I think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed to destruction."

When Pharaoh tried to wipe Musa (AS) and his people off the face of the earth, Allah drowned Pharaoh and his entire army together, and settled the Children of Israel in the land - proving that arrogant denial always ends in ruin.

deep_dives.title: The Spiritual Power and Status of the Surah
deep_dives.content:
Surah Al-Isra held a deeply cherished place in the nightly routine of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and his closest companions:

• The Prophet's Nightly Recitation: In a narration from Aisha (RA) recorded in Jami' at-Tirmidhi (2920), she stated: "The Prophet (pbuh) would not go to sleep until he had recited Surah Bani Israel (Al-Isra) and Surah Az-Zumar."
• An Ancient Treasure of the Companions: The great companion Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA) famously described Surah Al-Isra alongside four other Makkan chapters in Sahih al-Bukhari (4708, 4994), saying: "Surah Bani Israel, Al-Kahf, Maryam, Taha, and Al-Anbiya are among my earliest, finest earnings and my oldest treasures."
• The Quran as a Healing (Shifa'): In verse 82, this Surah also delivers a timeless spiritual promise: "And We send down of the Quran that which is healing and mercy for the believers." Classical scholars like Ibn Kathir explain that the Quran heals the heart from doubt, hypocrisy, and grief, and brings healing to the body by Allah's permission.

deep_dives.title: The Miraculous Night Journey (Al-Isra) and the Test of Faith (Verses 1 & 60)
deep_dives.content:
The Surah opens with Subhana ("Glory be to Allah") to highlight a miracle completely beyond human capability: taking Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) in a single night from the Sacred Mosque in Makkah to Al-Masjid al-Aqsa in Jerusalem.

The Tafsir and Hadith Details: Authentic Hadiths narrated by Anas ibn Malik (RA) in Sahih Muslim (162a) and Sahih al-Bukhari (3887) preserve the vivid details of that unforgettable night:

• Riding Al-Buraq to Jerusalem: Angel Jibril (AS) brought Al-Buraq, a white riding creature larger than a donkey and smaller than a mule, whose every stride reached as far as the eye could see. The Prophet (pbuh) rode it to Jerusalem, tied it to the ring used by earlier prophets, entered Al-Masjid al-Aqsa, prayed there, and led the prophets in prayer.
• The Choice of Milk: Jibril (AS) then presented him with two vessels - one containing wine and the other containing milk. The Prophet (pbuh) chose the milk, and Jibril (AS) smiled and said: "You have chosen the Fitrah (the pure, natural way)."
• The Ascension (Al-Mi'raj) and the Five Daily Prayers: From Jerusalem, the Prophet (pbuh) ascended through the seven heavens, greeting earlier prophets - Adam, Isa and Yahya, Yusuf, Idris, Harun, Musa, and Ibrahim (peace be upon them all) - until he reached Sidrat al-Muntaha (the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary). There, Allah spoke to him directly and gifted the Muslim Ummah the obligation of prayer, graciously reducing it from fifty daily prayers to five daily prayers carrying the full reward of fifty.
• The Morning Test in Makkah: When the Prophet (pbuh) returned to Makkah the same night and told the Quraysh, they mocked him wildly. In Sahih Muslim (172), the Prophet (pbuh) narrated that the disbelievers began grilling him about architectural details of Jerusalem that he had not memorized, causing him intense distress - until Allah miraculously raised an image of Jerusalem right before his eyes so he could describe every single gate and detail accurately. In Sahih al-Bukhari (3888, 4716), Ibn Abbas (RA) explicitly confirmed that the "vision" mentioned in verse 60 was a real, physical sight shown to the Prophet's own eyes that night, made as a test (fitnah) that separated sincere believers from stubborn mockers.

deep_dives.title: The Two Corruptions of the Children of Israel (Verses 2-8)
deep_dives.content:
Right after connecting Makkah to Jerusalem, Allah recounts the history of the previous caretakers of the Sacred Land - the Children of Israel (Bani Israel) - as a warning to every nation that holds religious authority.

The Tafsir Details: Allah gave Prophet Musa (AS) the Torah as a clear guide, reminding his people that they were descendants of the grateful believers saved on Prophet Nuh's Ark. Yet Allah decreed in their scripture that they would cause severe corruption on earth twice and rise to extreme arrogance.

Classical scholars like Ibn Kathir explain that when the first wave of corruption occurred - breaking Allah's laws and oppressing the righteous - Allah sent powerful, mighty enemies against them who marched right into their homes and overpowered them. Later, when they repented, Allah restored their strength, wealth, and numbers. Yet when they fell into arrogance and corruption a second time, enemies were again unleashed upon them to disgrace them, enter the Masjid in Jerusalem just as before, and destroy what they had built.

Allah closes this historical lesson with an open door of mercy and a clear warning: "It is expected that your Lord will have mercy upon you. But if you return [to corruption], We will return [to punishment]." True security never comes from bloodline or past glory; it comes only from obedience and justice.

deep_dives.title: The Arrogance of Iblis and His Limit Over True Servants (Verses 61-65)
deep_dives.content:
In the middle of the Surah, Allah returns to the very first act of pride in creation - explaining why human beings constantly face temptation and how they can defeat it.

The Tafsir Details: When Allah commanded the angels to prostrate to Prophet Adam (AS) out of honor, every single angel obeyed except Iblis. Blinded by pride, he arrogantly asked: "Should I prostrate to one You created from clay?" He then boasted to Allah that if given time until the Day of Resurrection, he would bring almost all of Adam's descendants under his control, except for a few.

Allah granted him respite and told him to use every tool he had: his "voice" (which classical scholars explain as every call to sin and disobedience), his "cavalry and infantry" (every human and jinn helper who spreads evil), and his partnership in "wealth and children" (unlawful earnings and raising children away from Allah's guidance). Yet Allah exposed the truth of Shaytan's schemes: "Satan does not promise them except delusion."

Then Allah gave believers the ultimate guarantee of safety in verse 65: "Indeed, over My true servants you have no authority. And sufficient is your Lord as a Disposer of affairs." Shaytan can whisper and invite, but he can never overpower a heart that sincerely relies on Allah.

deep_dives.title: Tahajjud and the Praised Station (Maqam Mahmud) (Verses 78-79)
deep_dives.content:
After outlining the times of the five daily prayers - highlighting that the dawn prayer (Fajr) is directly witnessed by the angels of the night and the day - Allah promises Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) an extraordinary honor reserved for him alone.

The Tafsir and Hadith Details: Allah commands the Prophet (pbuh) to rise during the night for the voluntary Tahajjud prayer, promising: "It is expected that your Lord will resurrect you to a praised station (Maqam Mahmud)."

In an authentic Hadith narrated by Abdullah ibn Umar (RA) and recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (4718), the Prophet (pbuh) explained what Maqam Mahmud is: on the terrifying Day of Resurrection, humanity will fall to their knees in distress, going from prophet to prophet - Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, and Isa (AS) - begging each one to intercede with Allah to begin the Judgment. Every prophet will apologize and decline until humanity reaches Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). He will step forward, fall in prostration before Allah's Throne, praise Allah with words inspired to him on that Day, and be granted the Grand Intercession (Ash-Shafa'ah al-'Uzma) - a station for which all of earlier and later creation will praise him.

deep_dives.title: The Question About the Soul (Ar-Ruh) (Verse 85)
deep_dives.content:
This verse captures a fascinating real-life encounter showing how Allah humiliates human arrogance by reminding us how tiny our knowledge truly is.

The Tafsir and Hadith Details: In an authentic Hadith narrated by Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA) and recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (125, 7297), Ibn Mas'ud was walking with the Prophet (pbuh) through a farm in Madinah while the Prophet leaned on a date-palm stalk. They passed by a group of Jewish scholars who whispered to one another: "Ask him about the Ruh (the soul/spirit)!" Some warned against asking, afraid he might give an answer they disliked, yet they went ahead and asked him.

The Prophet (pbuh) stood completely silent, leaning on the palm stalk, and Ibn Mas'ud realized immediately that revelation was descending upon him. Once the revelation finished, the Prophet (pbuh) recited verse 85:

• "And they ask you, [O Muhammad], about the soul (Ar-Ruh). Say, 'The soul is of the affair of my Lord. And mankind has not been given of knowledge except a little.'"*

Even with all human intellect and discovery, we cannot fully grasp the exact essence of the very soul keeping us alive - a humbling reminder that true knowledge belongs to Allah alone.

deep_dives.title: The Grand Finale: Calling Upon Allah and Ar-Rahman (Verses 110-111)
deep_dives.content:
Surah Al-Isra closes with a real-life Makkan incident about Allah's Beautiful Names, followed by one of the grandest declarations of pure monotheism in the entire Quran.

The Tafsir Details: Classical commentators like Ibn Kathir and Al-Tabari explain that in Makkah, the Prophet (pbuh) used to supplicate in prayer calling out "Ya Allah! Ya Rahman!" ("O Allah! O Most Merciful!"). A polytheist overheard him and mocked him to the Quraysh, saying: "Look at Muhammad - he forbids us from worshipping two gods, yet he himself is calling upon two gods: Allah and Ar-Rahman!"

Allah immediately revealed verse 110 to correct their ignorance forever: "Say, 'Call upon Allah or call upon Ar-Rahman (the Most Merciful). Whichever [name] you call - to Him belong the Best Names (Al-Asma' al-Husna).'" In the same verse, Allah also taught believers to keep a balanced, moderate voice in prayer - neither shouting loudly nor whispering silently.

Finally, verse 111 seals the entire chapter with majestic perfection:

• "And say, 'All praise is due to Allah, who has not taken a son and has had no partner in [His] dominion and has no [need of a] protector out of weakness; and glorify Him with [great] glorification.'"*

Surah Al-Isra carries the believer from the miraculous Night Journey that honored a grieving Prophet, through the timeless lessons of kindness to parents, human dignity, and Pharaoh's downfall, to the grand promise of Maqam Mahmud - opening with Subhana (glorifying Allah's power) and closing with Alhamdulillah and Takbir (praising and magnifying Him above every weakness or partner).
